Drone adoption and farm performance in smallholder rice farming: Evidence of adoption without adaptation from Vietnam’s Mekong Delta
abstract: While agricultural drones have demonstrated technical benefits in controlled experiments, their real-world adoption patterns and performance among smallholders remain underexplored. This study examines drone uptake and its economic impacts on rice farmers in Vietnam’s Mekong Delta, where commercial drone services have expanded rapidly in recent years. Using panel data from 756 seasonal observations across 387 households over six rice cropping seasons from 2022 to 2024, we employ generalised linear models and generalised linear mixed models to examine adoption determinants and linear mixed-effects models to assess farm performance outcomes. Results show that drone adoption is primarily determined by structural factors, farm size and local service availability, rather than farmer characteristics, such as education or training, whose effects are conditional on operational scale and disappear once household-level heterogeneity is accounted for. Drone adopters achieved modest yield (1.9%) and revenue (3.3%) gains, especially on smaller farms; however, higher spraying costs entirely offset these gains, resulting in no net improvement in profitability. Drone use did not reduce pesticide or fertiliser expenditures, revealing an “adoption without adaptation” pattern where technology uptake occurs largely without corresponding adjustments to input management practices. Additionally, larger farms adopt drones more readily, yet productivity and revenue benefits are concentrated on smaller farms, a structural paradox in technology diffusion. Since adoption alone does not ensure economic benefits, policies should bundle drone services with agronomic guidance and invest in cooperative-based delivery models to improve accessibility. Grounded in actual farming systems, this study advances evidence-based understanding of digital agricultural technology adoption under real-world conditions.

title: Estimating fine-scale soil moisture content and wheat yield in drought-heterogeneous farmlands using machine learning regressions on multispectral UAV imagery
abstract: With the development of precision agriculture, soil moisture content (SMC), a key factor affecting wheat yield, requires efficient and near real-time monitoring at the field scale. This study applies soil line indices derived from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery to estimate fine-scale SMC and wheat yield in two farmlands with distinct spatial SMC distributions (i.e., farmland drought heterogeneity) in Kinmen, Taiwan. By comparing traditional linear regression with several machine learning approaches, including support vector regression (SVR), gradient boosting regression (GBR), and convolutional neural network regression (CNNR), key indices contributing to SMC and yield estimation across different wheat growth stages were identified. The results indicate that both SMC and wheat yield can be reasonably explained when significant farmland drought heterogeneity is present. Linear regression achieved optimal coefficients of determination (p < 0.01) of 0.65 for SMC using the perpendicular vegetation index and 0.93 for wheat yield using the normalized difference vegetation index. Areas with higher SMC within a farmland were found to negatively affect wheat growth. Among the machine learning models, GBR and CNNR based on the selected indices (VAPDI and NDVI, respectively) achieved estimation accuracies of 98.0 % and 72.2 %, respectively, for total wheat yield across the two experimental farmlands. Temporal validation across different growing cycles suggests the potential for cross-year wheat yield prediction. Deviations from expected estimation patterns may be considered preliminary indicators of abnormal yield conditions, and early-stage yield estimation shows promising potential. Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence for early-stage yield prediction and offer valuable insights for optimizing irrigation timing and enhancing the development of AI-driven agricultural decision support systems.

title: Multi-sensor point cloud analysis for canopy volume estimation in a steep-slope Mediterranean vineyard: a comparison of LiDAR and RGB approaches
abstract: Volumetric analysis of tree canopies is increasingly important for farmers 4.0, as it enables the adoption of targeted agricultural practices. Additionally, the recent European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO) guideline introduced a new labelling system for plant protection products based on biometric indices as references to express the dose. Currently, conventional manual methods used for volumetric assessments are generally time-consuming. The present study aimed to undertake a comparative analysis of canopy volumes derived from various combinations of monitoring technologies and analytical methods applied to the point cloud, in conjunction with reference volumes obtained from manual measurements, within a highly complex scenario like the Mediterranean steep-slope vineyard. The technologies tested for UAV monitoring included LiDAR, low and high cost RGB cameras, whilst terrestrial monitoring was carried out with terrestrial LiDAR (GeoSLAM TM ). The analytical methods applied were alphashape (α = 0.1–0.5), convex hull, and voxelization (s = 0.05–0.10 m). The results showed that for UAV-based surveys, the convex hull was the most appropriate analytical method (RMSE: 0.10, 0.13, and 0.35 m 3 ), while for terrestrial LiDAR, the alpha shape with α = 0.5 was the most appropriate (RMSE: 0.10 m 3 ). Overall, the results showed that volumetric data can be obtained through rapid surveys, provided the most suitable analytical method is adopted.

title: Early crop type classification and mapping combining remote sensing and ancillary data
abstract: Accurate and timely crop type classification is critical for agricultural management and food security monitoring. Most existing approaches rely on the spectral response time series obtained from satellite imagery, primarily focusing on end-of-season classification. By providing accurate crop maps early in the season, policymakers, irrigation managers, and producer organizations can optimize water allocation, forecast production, and stabilize food prices. This study introduces a novel AI framework that integrates remote sensing data with ancillary information, such as cloud cover percentage, previous-year crop type, and irrigation type, for early crop type classification. The framework is validated on a dataset of approximately 130,000 fields in the region of Lleida, Catalonia (Spain), a representative Mediterranean agricultural landscape. Leveraging remote sensing data from the previous growing season enhanced early-stage classification performance, achieving an accuracy of approximately 70% at the season’s onset—a significant improvement over traditional approaches relying solely on current-season data. Ancillary data played a key role in mitigating challenges such as cloud-induced data gaps and limited spectral information and better predicting crop types in fields with permanent crops or no crop rotation. Incorporating ancillary data boosted accuracy by 10%, resulting in an overall accuracy of 80% early in the season, which increased to 88% by the season’s end. Despite these advancements, underrepresented crop classes remained difficult to classify accurately due to class imbalances, underscoring the need for improved dataset balancing techniques. The findings underscore the potential of integrating multi-source data to improve crop type classification, especially early in the season.

title: MFFT: an improved method for stable ID tracking and counting of multi-class mango segmentation with multi-feature fusion in complex occlusion scenarios
abstract: Accurate mango segmentation, counting, and biomass estimation are critical for orchard yield prediction. To address the challenges of low fruit segmentation accuracy, frequent ID switches, and large tracking and counting errors under complex occlusion scenarios, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion tracking method termed MFFT. The method is built on the Swin-T backbone and a customized Transformer decoder, integrated with shallow feature enhancement, boundary attention, and background gating modules. For mango segmentation, the proposed approach achieves 0.71 mIoU and 40.32 FPS for both on-tree and fallen mangoes. In the tracking stage, IOU, HSV, shape, and diagonal features are fused, together with an improved Kalman filter and ID lifecycle management, resulting in a MOTA of 0.6513 and a significant reduction in ID switches. The system innovatively introduces diagonal length as a computational metric, achieving a counting relative error of only 4.30% and a biomass estimation error of 4.49%. It outperforms mainstream algorithms such as Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, DTER, and ByteTrack across multiple metrics. The proposed method exhibits strong application potential in orchards and provides more precise data support and a decision-making foundation for digital agricultural production management. The code and dataset for this study have been made open source on Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UzvgiqlXn-C2aJZsHmcLAWSYaVYA0bnH/view?usp=sharing.

title: Research progress of autonomous navigation path planning methods for agricultural ground machinery: a review
Complementary-aware collaborative fusion: Advancing precise wheat lodging mapping using UAV-borne RGB imagery and LiDAR data

An automated High-Precision farm mapping pipeline using UAV point clouds
RaMor3D: adaptive registration and morphology-aware reconstruction for meat rabbits in confined spaces
Vision-based autonomous leaf-level spraying using wrist-inspired manipulators for integrated pest management in papaya greenhouses
abstract: Papaya plants exhibit complex canopy structures, which make spray application highly dependent on manual labour, requiring physical effort and considerable experience of the farmer. The shortage of skilled labour and the hazards of pesticide exposure further emphasise the need for automated precision spraying systems. This study presents an autonomous robotic sprayer (ARS) for precision spraying in papaya greenhouses and to support sustainable integrated pest management (IPM). The mechanical system was designed as a twin-sided mechanism with two degrees of freedom on each side, allowing it to mimic the key motions of the human wrist while maintaining mechanical simplicity and low production costs. The system is driven by an integrated leaf-segmentation module with depth-retrieval fusion and by a wrist exoskeleton that supplies motion-capture input. These inputs enable the system to reproduce the natural spraying motions of experienced farmers in the small-scale greenhouse. By integrating a Neutral Density filter with a depth-retrieval algorithm, the perception module sustains over 72 % leaf-recognition accuracy under greenhouse conditions. Compared with manual knapsack spraying, the proposed ARS reduced ground deposition by 39 % and improved spray coverage and uniformity across canopy layers. The system also achieved effective suppression of two major pests, two-spotted spider mite and silverleaf whitefly, confirming the biological relevance of the system. These results highlight the potential of ARS to reduce dependence on manual labour, minimise operator exposure, and enhance precision spraying in greenhouse cultivation.

title: A collaborative diffusion-VLM data synthesis framework for improving fine-grained cotton pest and disease classification
Editorial Board
Experimental study on flow field distribution and material separation characteristics in a pneumatic potato impurity removal device based on CFD-DEM coupling
Improved estimation of dissolved oxygen levels in commercial aquaculture using the ensemble Kalman filter
abstract: Dissolved oxygen is an essential environmental variable for Atlantic salmon in commercial aquaculture. Hypoxic conditions inhibit growth and increase the risk of mortality, leading to reduced welfare and profitability. Accurate and precise monitoring of dissolved oxygen levels is, therefore, a crucial aspect of optimal operation of aquaculture facilities. This has stimulated an ongoing research campaign seeking to utilise engineering cybernetic methodologies to improve oxygen estimation in commercial aquaculture. Previously, a mathematical model of the oxygen levels in sea-cages was developed based on the advection-diffusion equation. While this model estimated oxygen levels that matched those measured at a commercial site, its accuracy and precision would be greatly improved if it could assimilate real measurements into the estimation framework. Such an expansion would also help adapt the framework to future operational use, where measurements from a farm are assimilated into the framework in real time to provide a more accurate representation of the oxygen conditions therein. This study improves the previously developed oxygen estimation framework by applying the ensemble Kalman filter, a sequential Monte Carlo data assimilation method. The results are unambiguous since the filter implementation is more accurate and precise than the stand-alone oxygen model in both a practical and simulated setting. The estimation framework’s run rates are approximately 10 times faster than real-time on a standard laptop, enabling future deployment on the hardware setups commonly used at aquaculture facilities. This work represents a novel use of the ensemble Kalman filter and expands the frontier of environmental variable estimation in aquaculture.

title: Pest-induced damage detection in corn leaves using improved Faster R-CNN
abstract: Pest-induced damage detection in cereal crops, such as corn, is challenging because of the small and irregular nature of damage symptoms, which can closely resemble plant diseases or environmental stress and foreign-attached substances in leaves. Delays in identification or misdiagnosis can result in substantial yield and economic losses. Previous studies have primarily focused on pest species or diseases. This study presents a task-specific adaptation of Faster R-CNN for detecting pest-induced damage in corn leaves caused by Grasshoppers and Fall Armyworms by customising the RPN with parallel dilated convolutions and an adaptive attention module. A new field-collected corn leaf pest-induced damage dataset comprising 1,390 images, was annotated in collaboration with an agricultural expert. Forty images containing the artefact were embedded in the training dataset to enhance the model performance. The model was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, and four major evaluation metrics were evaluated. The introduction of the artefacts into the training data resulted in an improvement in mAP, along with a reduction in misdetections attributable to the artefacts. Furthermore, the incorporation of parallel dilated convolutions in the RPN of Faster R-CNN led to enhancements in mAP 50:95 (54.06%) and exhibited a high equilibrium between precision and recall, achieving an F1-score of 80.13% with increased computational cost. Compared with the baseline Faster R-CNN model, the proposed model achieved a +1.38-percentage point increase in recall for Fall Armyworm damage and a +1.79-percentage point improvement in mAP 50:95 for Grasshopper damage. This result suggests an improved detection of small objects (Fall Armyworms) and accurate localisation of larger, irregular objects (Grasshopper), both individually and when co-occurring. This research suggests a potential future applicability for farmers in the timely identification of pest infestations, thereby mitigating yield losses. These findings provide guidance for future research on detecting a wider variety of pest-induced crop damages across diverse geographical regions in agricultural computer vision applications.

title: Improving the cotton leaf area index estimation from multi-source remote sensing data based on ensemble learning model
Active and incremental learning with RAUNet for advancing soil cover monitoring from mobile digital imaging through deep learning
An automatic parameter search framework for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification by deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning
Behavioural phenotyping in red deer: Machine learning classification of accelerometer data from micro-movements to grazing
abstract: Monitoring deer behaviour continuously and objectively is essential for accurate welfare assessment in pastoral farming, yet conventional observation methods are labour-intensive and prone to subjective bias. We present an unsupervised machine-learning pipeline for classifying farmed red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) behaviour from wearable accelerometer data. Tri-axial accelerometers mounted on the head and ear of stags recorded movement at 50 Hz over 48 h. k -means clustering of the normalised signals yielded eight prototypical movements spanning three behavioural categories: inactive states (lying, resting with or without rumination/panting), grazing (stationary and walking), and rapid ear flicks. A first-order Markov chain then linked these prototypes into higher-order sequences we call ”super-prototypes”. These compound behaviours included ear-flick bouts and alternating grazing-stepping cycles. Within the single 24-h window, activity varied with time of day, ear flicks being markedly more frequent by day. Against independent video annotation, the eight categories agreed with the observer’s labelling at a mean of 0.96 across prototypes. Because classification reduces to a nearest-centroid operation, the algorithm runs on a 16 MHz microcontroller at over 4 × 1 0 8 classifications per second, four orders of magnitude faster than the sensor sampling rate. The pipeline requires no hand-labelled training data and runs in real time on the animal, a feasible basis for welfare monitoring in extensive deer farming systems once validated under field conditions.

title: Modeling the temperature–humidity coupling dynamics of soybean pod borer population and assessing the predictive performance of the PCM-NN algorithm
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and agricultural globalization, soybean production is increasingly threatened by pest outbreaks, with Leguminivora glycinivorella (commonly known as the soybean pod borer) being a major pest species. This pest is widely distributed, particularly in northeastern China, the country's primary soybean-producing region, where its outbreaks have significantly affected both yield and quality. Although statistical and mechanistic models have been applied to pest forecasting, existing approaches often fail to effectively integrate climatic factors with pest dynamics and lack sufficient expressive power. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel pest prediction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Specifically, we formulate a logistic-type ordinary differential equation (ODE) that incorporates microclimate factors, temperature, humidity, and time, to describe the temporal dynamics of the soybean pod borer population. This ODE model is embedded into the PINN framework to develop the Pest Correlation Model Neural Network (PCM-NN), which is used to jointly infer the microclimate-driven parameter function alpha(T, H, t) and fit the pest population dynamics. We evaluate PCM-NN using daily monitoring data of soybean pod borer collected in Changchun, Jilin Province, from July to September during 2020-2023. Experimental results demonstrate that PCM-NN preserves biological interpretability while exhibiting strong nonlinear representational capacity, offering a feasible pathway for pest modeling and forecasting under multi-factor climatic conditions. This approach provides valuable support for agricultural pest monitoring, prevention, and control strategies.

title: A conditional generative diffusion model enables joint retrieval of rice LAI and LCC
CVITrack-GDResYolo: An instance segmentation and tracking method for Pleurotus eryngii point clouds based on multi-view stereo vision
Multi-sensor integration and cloud-native AI for climate-smart agricultural monitoring: A systems framework
abstract: Climate change intensifies drought, heat stress, and production instability, requiring scalable monitoring systems to support climate-smart agriculture. Remote sensing has evolved into operational decision-support infrastructure enabled by open-access satellite archives, multi-sensor integration, cloud-native computing, and machine learning. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature (2000–2025) and proposes a unified five-layer computational framework for agricultural climate adaptation. The framework integrates data acquisition, cloud processing, machine learning analytics, data fusion, and decision-support outputs into end-to-end workflows. The synthesis is based on a structured review of 120 core peer-reviewed studies, complemented by additional foundational and methodological references to ensure technical depth. Comparative evidence indicates that multi-sensor fusion enhances robustness relative to single-source approaches. Optical-radar integration using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 has achieved classification accuracies of up to 89 % in cloud-prone regions, compared to approximately 76 % using optical data alone. ML-based yield prediction models frequently improve performance by 5–20 % in R 2 relative to empirical regression under data-rich conditions, while multi-temporal ML approaches enable detection of crop stress 2–4 weeks before visible symptoms occur. However, ML superiority over process-based models is conditional on calibration quality, data availability, and cross-regional transferability. Cloud-based platforms have reduced computational barriers and enabled large-scale time-series analysis, supporting operational monitoring from field to regional scales. Despite these advances, reproducibility limitations, ground-truth data scarcity, and reduced transferability across agroecological zones remain significant constraints, particularly in smallholder-dominated systems. Advancing climate-smart agricultural monitoring therefore depends not only on improved sensing technologies, but on interoperable, reproducible, and transferable computational frameworks capable of delivering reliable decision support across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes.

title: Corrigendum to “Accurate localization of fruit targets and picking points with multi-dimensional attention and dynamic upsampling”, [Comput. Electr. Agr. 240 (2026) 111211 doi: 10.1016/j.compag.2025.111211]
A dataset for investigating dust removal for person detection
abstract: Autonomous agricultural machinery must be able to operate safely in harsh conditions, such as dust. Dust raised during tillage can obscure objects such as an approaching person, thus posing a safety risk. One way to cope with this is to remove the dust from the image data, thereby increasing the detectability of the person. Hence, this study investigates the extent to which dust removal improves person detection. A dataset containing real-world dusty and dust-free images is presented and enriched with synthetic dusty images. To achieve this, dust was added synthetically to the dust-free images. The developed method recreates the temporal formation of dust during tillage and its influence by wind. Subsequently, state-of-the-art image dehazing and translation methods were benchmarked on the dataset. Additionally, a YOLO11 model was utilized for person detection and trained on different dataset configurations. Training on synthetic dusty images increased detection performance, measured in terms of mAP, by 55.11 percentage points compared to a pretrained detection network. Furthermore, combining synthetic and real-world dusty images increased mAP by 2.78 percentage points compared to training on real-world dusty images alone. Moreover, dust removal improved the detection performance in heavy dusty conditions by 27.23 percentage points compared to a pretrained network. More importantly, the combination of a dust removal method and a retrained YOLO11 on the specific output of the dust removal method outperformed a YOLO11 trained on real-world dusty images by 3.39 percentage points in heavy dusty conditions. The results highlight the potential to enhance the safety of autonomous agricultural machinery by removing dust from images prior to detection.

title: Novel traceability strategy based on redactable blockchain for food supply chain
abstract: In recent years, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing the security and transparency of food traceability systems. However, challenges such as data immutability, privacy concerns, and regulatory compliance have limited its widespread adoption. To address these issues, we propose a novel food traceability strategy that integrates redactable blockchain technology with attribute-based encryption. The strategy enables secure and efficient data editing, fine-grained access control, and distributed storage, ensuring the integrity and privacy of food traceability data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves transaction execution time, transaction per second (TPS), and data transmission efficiency compared to existing solutions. This research contributes to the development of more secure, flexible, and scalable food traceability systems, with potential applications in enhancing food safety and supply chain transparency.

Leaf- and canopy-level hyperspectral sensing of wheat-Fusarium head blight-Trichoderma gamsii interactions
abstract: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is a major mycotoxigenic disease of wheat, causing yield and quality losses and deoxynivalenol contamination. Rapid, non-destructive tools are needed to detect FHB, monitor wheat physiological responses, and evaluate sustainable management strategies, including biological control agents. Although vegetation spectroscopy is widely used for high-throughput phenotyping, most spectral studies focus on binary disease detection, while the capacity of hyperspectral data to capture concurrent host–pathogen–biocontrol responses across leaf and canopy scales remains underexplored. Here, we tested a full-range (400–2400 nm) hyperspectral phenotyping framework to track early interactions among winter wheat, FHB, and Trichoderma gamsii T6085. Two cultivars, Bingo and Rebelde, with higher and lower FHB susceptibility, respectively, were treated with a chemical fungicide (Chem) or T. gamsii T6085 (Bioc) under FHB pressure. Leaf- and canopy-level spectra were acquired at 2, 5, and 14 days post-inoculation, alongside gas exchange, water status, and chlorophyll measurements. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) tested whole-spectrum effects, partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) explored class separability, and partial least squares regression (PLSR) estimated physiological traits. PERMANOVA detected genotype × inoculation × treatment interactions from 5 days post-inoculation at leaf and canopy levels. PLS-DA revealed treatment- and cultivar-dependent spectral fingerprints, but overall low-to-fair validation performance indicates that these class-specific patterns should be interpreted as exploratory and not as evidence of operational treatment discrimination. PLSR provided high accuracy for chlorophyll content and osmotic potential, moderate accuracy for CO 2 -assimilation traits, and poor accuracy for transpiration and leaf water potential. While the workflow is scalable as an experimental and analytical framework, its operational deployment will require broader validation across sites, seasons, cultivars, disease-pressure conditions, and sensing platforms.

title: A Knowledge-Driven Cross-Modal fusion method for intelligent quality assessment of cabbage
Deep transfer learning for spectral prediction of kiwifruit quality across cultivars and instruments
Plant wearables in smart agriculture: advancements, technical challenges, opportunities, and a cyber-physical roadmap in volatile organic compound detection
abstract: The agricultural sector faces escalating challenges from climate-induced abiotic stressors, herbivory, and pathogens. Optimizing crop productivity requires advanced technologies for real-time monitoring. While volatile organic compounds (VOCs) serve as early-onset biomarkers for plant stress, conventional laboratory methods lack high-temporal resolution, and portable electronic noses suffer from limited selectivity. However, transitioning to in situ plant wearables is severely bottlenecked by critical research gaps: severe signal baseline drift caused by fluctuating ambient humidity crosstalk, stomatal shielding from non-porous substrates that disrupts natural leaf transpiration, and a computational void in deploying artificial intelligence for autonomous material stoichiometry optimization and real-time deconvolution of overlapping VOC profiles at the resource-constrained edge. To critically address these gaps, this review systematizes the transition toward Cyber-Physical Plant Systems (CPPS) via wearable VOC-sensing architectures. We evaluate the AI-material nexus, demonstrating how metaheuristic optimization and Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks like SHAP and LIME can autonomously optimize sensor materials and validate biogenic fingerprints. A central contribution of this work is a transdisciplinary and strategic four-phase technical roadmap integrating materials science, edge-computing, and Industry 5.0 principles. This framework outlines the engineering of transpirational-neutral architectures and low-power Edge-AI hardware to resolve multi-stressor profiles. By bridging the gap between plant metabolism and digital intelligence, this review provides a strategic pathway aligning with Agriculture 5.0 to build autonomous bio-information systems for enhanced agricultural resilience.

title: Spatiotemporal video encoder integrated with metadata fusion for action recognition and behavior analysis
abstract: Automated behavior monitoring and action recognition is challenging in dense, dynamic environments of broiler pens, combined with the challenges of handheld smartphone footage. This study developed and validated an integrated pipeline for spatiotemporal action recognition and behavioral analysis of individual broiler chickens using smartphone-captured video. Our end-to-end framework addresses key technical challenges by first stabilizing raw footage to correct motion artifacts, then employing YOLOv11-Pose for robust detection and pose estimation in crowded scenes, and ByteTrack for multi-object tracking. The core innovation is a novel metadata fusion strategy, where spatiotemporal features from an X3D video encoder were integrated with pose-derived contextual metadata (such as velocity and proximity to feeders and drinkers) using a multilayer perceptron. This intermediate fusion approach enabled the model to disambiguate visually similar but contextually distinct actions, such as drinking versus feeding. The system demonstrated strong performance on five key maintenance behaviors (resting, walking, standing, drinking, and eating), achieving an average F1-score of 0.864 and an overall test accuracy of 86.41 %. The system was particularly effective at detecting drinking and feeding behaviors, with individual F1-scores of 0.949 (94 % accuracy) and 0.928 (91.89 % accuracy) respectively. The system successfully processed 174 videos, producing valuable insights in the form of behavioral metrics, spatial heatmaps, and individual trajectories. This demonstrates that an integrated system, combining stabilization, advanced multi-task models, and contextual metadata fusion, can effectively use smartphone footage to create a scalable, objective tool for precision poultry farming and welfare research. The key advantages of the proposed framework include its ability to disambiguate visually similar birds and behavior actions through metadata fusion, its use of accessible cost-effective smartphone data, and its balance of accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: SPROUT: AI-based seedling emergence PRedictiOn and trait extraction using RGB time-series
abstract: Early crop establishment strongly influences plant performance and yield, making seedling emergence an important trait in crop phenotyping, breeding, and stress physiology studies. However, emergence monitoring is still commonly performed manually and typically records only the final emergence percentage, limiting the analysis to other dynamic observations. Automated image-based approaches are promising but remain challenging due to the small size of plant structures, heterogeneous soil backgrounds, and variability across imaging systems. Here, we present SPROUT (AI- based S eedling PR edicti O n and trait extraction U sing RGB T ime-series), a low-cost RGB imaging pipeline for automated prediction of crop emergence dynamics and trait extraction. The system integrates instance segmentation, object-detection–based data reduction, and temporal deep learning to estimate the emergence time of individual seedlings from RGB image sequences. The pipeline then automatically reconstructs emergence curves and extracts associated traits, including final emergence percentage, EC50, and emergence synchronicity. SPROUT was developed and evaluated using barley and wheat datasets acquired with different RGB cameras under controlled growth-chamber conditions. In the development and retraining settings, the best-performing TCN model achieved 90.0% per-well accuracy with a ± 2h tolerance, supporting accurate emergence curve reconstruction. In an independent inference-only dataset, the model still captured approximate emergence dynamics, although accuracy decreased to 59.3%, indicating that SPROUT is best used as a modular pipeline that can be retrained or fine-tuned for new crop, camera, or experimental domains. A cadmium-stress case study in two contrasting wheat genotypes showed that SPROUT-derived traits captured genotype-specific establishment strategies associated with growth and metabolic responses.

title: A robust rank aggregation based interpretable minimum predictor set for scalable soil organic carbon mapping
Robust autonomous navigation in unstructured orchards: Integrated LIO-SAM with NDT-based relocalization and Bayesian traversability mapping
Three-dimensional reconstruction and light interception quantification of maize/soybean system based on UAV cross-surround photography
abstract: [Background and objective] Maize/soybean intercropping performance is strongly influenced by three-dimensional (3D) canopy architecture, which regulates light interception and crop complementarity. This study aimed to reconstruct field maize/soybean canopies from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery and quantify how planting pattern and density affect canopy light distribution, yield, and land equivalent ratio (LER). [Method] Field experiments were conducted in northeast China using three row configurations (2:2, 2:4, and 4:4 maize/soybean strips) and three maize planting densities (6.4 × 104, 9.6 × 104, and 11.2 × 104 plants ha⁻1). Canopy structure was reconstructed using UAV RGB cross-surround imaging, structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo (SfM-MVS), and point-cloud processing. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated using plant height, leaf length, and leaf width. The Helios light model was used to simulate canopy light interception and distribution. [Results] Plant height estimation achieved R2 values of 0.92 for maize and 0.72 for soybean, while leaf length and width estimates achieved R2 ≥ 0.88 and relative root mean square errors of 5–10 %. Helios simulations showed treatment-specific differences in canopy light distribution. At 102 days after emergence, maize light interception rate in medium-density 2:2 and 2:4 treatments exceeded 600 W m⁻2 during peak sunlight hours, whereas high-density treatments increased soybean shading. Medium-density treatments showed a favorable numerical balance between light capture and crop complementarity, with LER values of 1.06 ± 0.16 for 2:2M and 1.00 ± 0.04 for 4:4M; however, total LER was not significantly affected by planting density. [Conclusion] UAV RGB cross-surround imaging combined with SfM-MVS reconstruction and light-interception modeling provides an effective workflow for linking 3D canopy architecture, light acquisition, and yield formation. Medium-density configurations showed a favorable numerical balance between canopy light capture and interspecific complementarity.

title: PanicleScope-Net: A small-object-aware network for rice panicle segmentation in complex field scenes
Comprehensive low-damage mechanical weeding technology considering the spatial distribution of crop roots: A case study of maize farmland
An appearance-independent multi-object tracking framework for group-housed pigs
Long-term identity-consistent multi-pig tracking in group-housed pens
Bovine-LTID: A vision-based spatio-temporal identity system for multi-camera cattle tracking and long-term behavior monitoring
abstract: Multi-camera video monitoring of group-housed cattle is essential for health assessment in precision livestock farming, offering a scalable, non-invasive alternative to labor-intensive manual observations and restrictive wearable sensors. However, existing systems for cross-camera identity matching typically rely on computationally intensive appearance-based Re-identification (ReID). These approaches often struggle in dense barns due to frequent mutual occlusions, viewpoint variations, and the high visual similarity of cattle coat patterns. To address these limitations, we propose Bovine Long-Term Identity (Bovine-LTID), a resource-efficient, ReID-embedding-free spatio-temporal tracking framework for multi-camera behavior monitoring. Instead of relying on ambiguous appearance features, Bovine-LTID maintains identity consistency through spatial geometry and temporal logic. The system integrates a behavior-aware detector (YOLOv9s) with a cattle-optimized single-view tracker (CowTracker) to recover identities during prolonged occlusions. For cross-view synchronization, trajectories are projected into a unified ground-plane coordinate system via homography calibration and managed by a centralized Global ID Pool. Trained on NVIDIA H200 GPU, the detection module achieves a test-set mAP50 of 0.944, while the complete pipeline operates at approximately 13 FPS on consumer-grade hardware (NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop, 8 GB VRAM). The cross-camera fusion mechanism reduces global raw identity switches by 87.6% over single-camera baselines and achieves a 99.33% cross-view identity consistency. These findings present a practical methodology for scalable, automated herd welfare assessment spanning from high-performance training to edge deployment.

title: FedAD: Federated learning with generative data augmentation and adaptive parameter decomposition for rice pest and disease identification
DASNet: Dual-channel adaptive segmentation network for pigtail fork bone path generation
TreePMNet: a deep matching network for registration of UAV and handheld LiDAR data in fine phenotyping of rubber plantations
abstract: Advanced phenotyping is essential for precise growth monitoring and reliable yield forecasting of economically significant rubber trees. Unmanned laser scanning (ULS) from an aerial perspective and handheld laser scanning (HLS) from the ground can efficiently capture 3D structural information of rubber plantations. Registering these two datasets can compensate for respective information gaps and achieve a more complete 3D representation. However, existing point cloud registration methodologies often suffer from low robustness or computational inefficiency when applied to forest scenes. This study proposes TreePMNet, a deep learning-based point cloud registration method. First, a Local Feature Aggregation (LFA) module is designed to generate salient keypoints and distinctive descriptors. Subsequently, a Progressive Transformation Estimation (PTE) module is used to achieve coarse-to-fine registration. The proposed method was evaluated using the public ULS-HLS-Rubber dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that TreePMNet facilitates both effective and efficient registration of ULS and HLS point clouds. The average RMSE, RRE, and RTE values reached 0.09 m, 0.17°, and 0.22 m, respectively. Furthermore, the average processing time for a 900 m 2 plot was only 0.98 s. The R 2 values for tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), and crown diameter extracted from the registered point cloud data reached 0.989, 0.856, and 0.914, respectively. This study underscores the developmental potential of deep learning-based methods for ULS and HLS point cloud registration in complex forest environments. Our findings provide invaluable support for the accurate acquisition of 3D structural information and advanced phenotypic characterization in rubber plantations.

title: A novel test methodology for evaluating prescription-map-based ISOBUS variable rate sprayers in viticulture
abstract: The use of variable rate application (VRA) technology enables spatial- and demand-oriented application of plant protection products, thereby facilitating precise and efficient plant protection in viticulture. However, there is a lack of standardised test methods for validating dynamic application volume rates for VRA sprayers in specialty crops. This paper presents a test methodology to evaluate the performance of ISOBUS-compliant VRA sprayers using prescription maps by comparing prescribed and applied spray volumes under controlled test bench and real field conditions. Therefore, four different test scenarios were developed for both environments to enable a systematic assessment of dynamic variable rate behaviour, including fixed (Scenario 1) and variable application volume rates under varying driving speeds (Scenario 2) and prescribed volume rate levels (Scenario 3). Depending on the scenario, the applied spray volumes derived from manual reference measurements, ISOBUS task logs and external flow sensor data (Scenario 4) were compared with each other. Overall, the developed test scenarios offer a first structured approach to assess the performance of VRA sprayers under controlled test bench and field conditions. In the first three scenarios, RMSE values below 5 % indicate that manual reference measurements and ISOBUS task log data provide a consistent and reproducible basis for assessing VRA behaviour along entire vine rows. In contrast, flow measurements using external sensors positioned downstream of the PWM nozzles showed higher deviations (RMSE ≤ 7.7 %) under highly dynamic conditions, demonstrating limitations for accurate applied spray volume assessment in the present experimental configuration.

title: C2BPNet: a crop disease segmentation network based on context-content-boundary perception
Design and experiment of a collision warning system for unmanned tractors based on real-time trajectory prediction
Research on adaptive denoising methods and characteristic analysis of load signals in agricultural tractors
Numerical simulation of the effect of exhaust fan layout on indoor air quality in stacked-cage poultry buildings during winter
Application research on the mechanism of antlion vibration for reducing resistance and energy consumption in subsoiler
abstract: Subsoiling operations can effectively break the plow pan of the soil, thereby improving soil structure and promoting root growth and water infiltration. However, subsoiling operation faces challenges such as high resistance and high energy consumption, especially at the front of the subsoiler is prone to form large soil nuclei, resulting in a sharp increase in resistance. In this study, a high-frequency controllable vibration mechanism inspired by antlion biology for subsoiling resistance reduction and energy consumption reduction, is proposed, aiming to reduce resistance and saving energy during subsoiling operations by adjusting the vibration frequency. Through the derivation of the theoretical model, we systematically analysed the effects of various parameters in the subsoiling process on the reduction of resistance and energy consumption of controlled vibratory subsoiling, and further field experiments not only verified the validity of the theoretical model, but also visually demonstrated the significant resistance reduction effect of high-frequency vibration in actual subsoiling operation. The results show that the theoretical model of vibratory subsoiling operation can better reflect the actual subsoiling resistance, and illustrate the resistance reduction and energy consumption reduction effect of high-frequency controlled vibration subsoiling operation. The vibration subsoiling was able to reduce resistance by more than 20% compared with a subsoiler without a vibration source, with only a slight increase in energy. The results of the study provide a new idea for the resistance reduction design of subsoiler, and play a certain guiding significance for the vibration resistance reduction design of other soil-engaging components.

title: Intelligent integration in agricultural insect management equipment: applications, challenges, and future directions
Satellite-anchored UAV sensing system for high-resolution soil moisture mapping
DEM-MBD coupled simulation for quantifying seedbed compaction and wheat emergence force during post-sowing wheat compaction
Quantification of group and individual behavioural responses to a nutritional challenge in dairy goats
abstract: Monitoring individual animal behaviour using sensor technology provides valuable insights into adaptation to environmental challenges. This study investigates the effects of a controlled nutritional challenge on the behavioural patterns of dairy goats using accelerometer-derived behavioural data. Fourteen goats were equipped with collar-mounted accelerometers for 19 days, including two days of nutritional challenge in the middle. The challenge consisted of a 7-day control period with standard total mixed ration (TMR), 2 days of straw feeding only, and a 10-day recovery period on the TMR. The ACT4Behav pipeline was used to classify behaviour from accelerometer data, and multiple features were extracted to characterize activity profiles. Post-challenge behaviours were compared to pre-challenge ones, considered as baseline. At the group level, mixed linear model analysis showed that rumination time decreased during the nutritional challenge, while time spent with the head in the feeder increased, particularly during the day. Lying time remained unchanged during the day but increased at night. At the individual level, high variability in behavioural responses was observed. Two novel indices, the Challenge Effect Index (CEI) and the Recovery Index (RI), were introduced to characterise the diversity of behavioural responses and recovery strategies among goats. While some goats fully recovered their baseline behavioural patterns, others exhibited higher levels of certain behaviours after the challenge. These results demonstrate that group-level analyses are not sufficient to assess the impact of environmental challenges, as individuals may have different response strategies.

title: Modelling the shapes of agricultural materials in DEM: methods, advances, and challenges

AgrospAI: A data space for sovereign data sharing and on-demand AI services in agriculture
abstract: Digital transformation in agriculture is often hindered by stakeholders’ reluctance to share sensitive operational data. While regulatory pressures for environmental sustainability increase, farmers lack tools to demonstrate compliance without relinquishing control over their data. This paper presents AgrospAI, an agricultural data space demonstrator that is designed to ensure data sovereignty by design. Unlike traditional platforms that require data transfer, AgrospAI utilizes a “Compute-to-Data” (C2D) paradigm. We first demonstrate this via a high-value use case in the Spanish pig farming sector: a sovereign workflow for environmental certification. This system enables farmers to generate verifiable compliance reports while keeping raw sensor data localized and private. Additionally, we showcase a second use case: an on-demand semantic mapping that lowers entry barriers for heterogeneous data sources, allowing data to be shared as-is and mapped and integrated when needed. Our results indicate that AgrospAI provides an environment designed to support trust in which data providers remain sovereign, even when integrating data from diverse sources, and consumers receive actionable insights (e.g., sustainability scores) without ever accessing the providers’ underlying raw datasets. This helps mitigate the risks of data leakage and unauthorized reuse, may help address some of the barriers that hinder data sharing, and enables value generation from data that would otherwise remain unused.

Technology Acceptance Level (TAL): A human-centred metric for evaluating trustworthy artificial intelligence in agriculture
abstract: Artificial intelligence ( AI ) systems are increasingly proposed for agricultural decision support, precision farming and precision livestock farming ( PLF ), yet large-scale and durable adoption by practitioners remains the exception rather than the rule. Established maturity scales such as the Technology Readiness Level ( TRL ) capture the engineering progression of a technology from basic principles to operational deployment, but they are agnostic to whether end users actually rely on the resulting system in their daily work. This paper introduces the Technology Acceptance Level ( TAL ) as a complementary, human-centred metric for evaluating the usability, trustworthiness and operational uptake of AI in agriculture. TAL is defined as a nine-level ordinal scale, anchored in the Technology Acceptance Model and the European Union ethics guidelines for Trustworthy AI , that captures the trajectory from initial exposure of a system to a practitioner up to its stable, autonomous integration into routine decision-making. Each level is operationalised by a small set of measurable criteria spanning perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, transparency, reliability under changing conditions, and alignment with agricultural workflows. We provide a mathematically grounded aggregation rule based on a non-compensatory, minimum-of-dimensions principle that prevents a single weak dimension from being masked by strong scores elsewhere, and we derive a confidence interval for TAL estimates from practitioner survey data. The framework is illustrated through three representative use cases — variable-rate nitrogen management in arable cropping, vision-based fruit detection for selective harvesting, and computer-vision-based lameness detection in dairy cattle — each a distinct agricultural AI system, chosen to demonstrate how systems of comparable engineering maturity can occupy very different acceptance levels and, in particular, how the dimension that limits acceptance differs systematically across deployment contexts. By explicitly addressing the human-in-the-loop, TAL is proposed as a diagnostic instrument — subject to empirical validation — for identifying adoption barriers, prioritising iterative system improvement, and steering the transition from technically functional prototypes to practically accepted, trustworthy AI in the agri-food sector. The framework is developed and illustrated within a high-income, European-influenced agricultural context, and its scores in this article are illustrative rather than empirically measured. Two limitations bound these claims and should be read alongside them: the framework has not yet been validated against field data, and it is scoped to decision-support and monitoring AI , so that systems relying on physical actuation — and settings beyond the Western commercial context in which it was developed — require further extension.

Toward intelligent pig farming: Advancing health and welfare monitoring through computer vision–based behavioral analysis
abstract: Modern pig production is increasingly moving toward smart and intelligent farming systems, integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence for precision management. Camera-based computer vision has emerged as a promising non-contact sensing tool for monitoring pig health and welfare through behavioral analysis, given the strong association between behavioral patterns and physiological status. Following a PRISMA-based search, 45 studies were included for critical synthesis on computer vision-based behavioral analysis in pigs, with emphasis on detectable behavioral indicators, imaging configurations, model architectures, post-processing strategies, and deployment constraints. Findings show that posture and nutritive behaviors are the most mature targets for monitoring because they are visually distinctive, biologically informative, and compatible with lightweight object-detection pipelines. In contrast, aggression, biting, enrichment interaction, suckling, and individual activity metrics require stronger temporal modeling, segmentation, or multi-object tracking, which increases annotation burden, computational cost, and susceptibility to occlusion and identity errors. Recent pig-specific modifications to YOLO, transformer-inspired, segmentation, and tracking models have improved performance through attention mechanisms, multi-scale feature fusion, occlusion-aware regression, lightweight convolution, and detector-tracker coupling. However, high reported accuracies often reflect controlled datasets rather than commercial robustness. Critical barriers include limited multi-farm validation, inconsistent annotation and post-processing rules, insufficient anomaly-detection thresholds, weak long-term identity preservation, and hardware constraints for edge deployment. Future efforts should prioritize developing standardized benchmarks, biologically grounded behavioral metrics, explainable and domain-adaptive artificial intelligence, and edge-ready architectures that convert model outputs into interpretable management alerts. This review provides a deployment-oriented framework for advancing computer vision from experimental behavior recognition toward scalable behavioral monitoring and intelligent decision support in pig production systems.

A lightweight DDC-YOLO and inspection-robot system for dead broiler detection in caged broiler houses
abstract: In caged broiler houses, dead-broiler detection typically relies on manual inspection, which is labor-intensive, inefficient, and difficult for high-level cages. To address these problems, this study proposed an automatic detection system for dead broilers in cage environments and deployed it on an inspection-robot platform for automated monitoring. First, to mitigate complex lighting and image blur, Gamma transform and Gaussian blur were applied for data augmentation to simulate real breeding scenes and improve model robustness. Second, the DDC-YOLO (DeadChicken-YOLO) detection model was developed; it uses a UIB lightweight backbone, the WIoU loss, the SimAM attention mechanism, and a DBFF feature-fusion module to enhance feature extraction and target detection while reducing model complexity, combined with TensorRT on edge devices to accelerate inference. Finally, a self-iterative mechanism was implemented that links robot data collection and detection with cloud-based transfer learning and model backhaul updates so the model could continuously adapt to new scenarios, such as different broiler breeds after deployment. The experimental results showed that the proposed DDC-YOLO achieved a precision of 96.8%, a recall of 85.4%, an F1 score of 90.8%, and mAP@0.5 of 93.1%. Compared with the original YOLO11, the model reduced parameters by 1.437 M and decreased size by 2.8 MB. In real farm environments, the model achieved real-time, accurate detection of dead broiler chickens with the continuous migration and adaptation across broiler-breed scenarios. Overall, the proposed method balanced detection accuracy, edge-deployment capability, and continuous optimization potential, and it can provide technical support for unmanned and reduced-staff broiler cage farming.

Real-Time Automated Body Condition Scoring of Dairy Cows in a Commercial Rotary Milking Parlor Using RGB-D Two-Stream Deep Learning
abstract: Automated body condition scoring (BCS) can improve the frequency, objectivity, and decision-making value of dairy cow monitoring, but its deployment in commercial rotary milking parlors remains challenging because animals are imaged under continuous flow, variable posture, changing backgrounds, and strict real-time constraints. This study presents a deployment-oriented RGB-D framework for automated BCS estimation during routine milking in a commercial rotary parlor. Synchronized RGB and depth images were acquired with an overhead Kinect sensor during three daily milking sessions, while RFID-triggered acquisition linked each image pair to individual cow identity. Expert reference scores were assigned using the Ferguson five-point BCS protocol with 0.25-unit increments. After quality control, the dataset comprised 25,700 RGB-D image pairs from 1,025 lactating cows. The proposed pipeline integrates YOLOv26l-based cow localization, RGB-D region-of-interest alignment, pad-and-resize preprocessing, and continuous BCS regression using a Two-Stream ResNet18 architecture with late feature fusion. Performance was assessed using an animal-wise split and compared with single-modality and alternative backbone models. The Two-Stream ResNet18 achieved the best performance, with MAE = 0.076, Accuracy0 = 83.6 %, Accuracy0.25 = 95.76 %, and Accuracy0.50 = 99.35 %, while maintaining an end-to-end latency of 95.0 ms. By combining RFID-linked RGB-D sensing, modality-aligned fusion, and low-latency inference, the framework enables automated BCS estimation under routine commercial rotary milking conditions. The resulting industrial-scale RGB-D dataset provides a reproducible benchmark for future precision dairy monitoring systems.

Autonomous Tissue-Interfaced Plant-Machine Interface for Real-Time Physiological Control of Phosphate
abstract: The emergence of smart agriculture has motivated the development of smart fertigation management system (FMS) to replace conventional scheduled-meter-based fertigation. For smart agriculture, these new FMS should possess five key characteristics: robotic, in vivo microneedle-based electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) sensing; machine-learning (ML)-based instant data interpretation; automated precise nutrient formulation and delivery; real-time feedback-driven fertigation adjustment; and identified optimal growth phosphate status. However, sensors, ML, or automated fertigation injector reported to date typically fulfill one or two requirements at the same time, and rare are examples of FMSs that fulfill all five requirements simultaneously. Here, we present a bio-integrated computerized FMS that meet all five requirements simultaneously. TheMobile Sensing Platform provides stable, high-throughput measurements (16 plants/h) with minimal tissue disruption, with equipped MN sensors accessing into plant compartments to enable instant detection of physiological phosphate status; the lightweight Extra Trees classifier translated impedance spectra into plant phosphate states with 89% accuracy in <1s; These predictions triggered automated nutrient formulation and delivery within 15 min and 0.25 g/L precision, demonstrating continuous electronic-biological feedback control. Deployment in indoor strawberry cultivation identified an optimal phosphate regime that improved yield while reducing fertilizer input relative to conventional recommendations. By bridging the gap between tissue-interfaced sensing and closed-loop actuation, this work establishes a prototype of potentially scalable bioelectronic framework that couples living plant physiology with autonomous electronics, unlocking new avenues for sustainable, bio-integrated automation in smart agriculture

title: Leaf pigment profiling for sensitive detection of nutrient deficiency syndromes in strawberry
PRISM: A methodological framework for reproducible data-to-model translation in spatial crop modeling
abstract: Process-based crop models are increasingly applied to forecast yields and assess climate risks in rainfed smallholder agriculture across sub-Saharan Africa. However, the prerequisite step of transforming heterogeneous agricultural data into standardized, model-ready inputs remains a major challenge for reproducible and comparable spatial crop modeling. Here we present PRISM (Platform-Ready Inputs for Spatial Modeling), a framework that formalizes data retrieval, quality control, gap-filling, spatial harmonization, and format conversion to produce standardized input packages compatible with multiple crop modeling frameworks. PRISM separates agronomic specifications from model-specific settings, with provenance records documenting preparation decisions. Case studies across four crop modeling frameworks in Mali, Niger, Nigeria, and Senegal demonstrated that all generated packages loaded without manual editing and that simulated outputs fell within published benchmark ranges. By automating the data-to-model translation process, PRISM enables systematic data preparation for spatial crop modeling across platforms in data-scarce regions, facilitating multi-model comparison studies for yield estimation, climate impact assessment, and agricultural planning.

title: LCSNet–FedPerGC: An efficient federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification in the Mekong Delta

Development of a two-step cross-cultivar grape quality prediction model using outdoor hyperspectral imaging in three grape cultivars: Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner
abstract: Sensing technologies that are independent of berry-color variation across grape cultivars, particularly under varying environmental stress conditions, are crucial for advancing precision viticulture. This study developed a two-step cross-cultivar quality prediction model for three grape cultivars with red or white berries—Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner—using an outdoor hyperspectral camera (HSC). We introduce a seamless soft-clustering approach that groups spectral characteristics without prior cultivar labels, using a coefficient-boosting method integrated with two dimensionality-reduction techniques: principal component analysis (PCA) and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). For Brix prediction across the three grape cultivars, the R 2 values were 0.72 (normal model), 0.75 (PCA-boosted), and 0.83 (UMAP-boosted); for pH prediction, the values were 0.70, 0.75, and 0.82, respectively. UMAP-boosted models consistently outperformed the normal model (without boosting), and PCA-boosted models also improved performance. While both the normal and PCA-boosted models improved performance, the UMAP-boosted models demonstrated superior accuracy for Brix and pH across both single- and cross-cultivar settings suggesting that UMAP more effectively captures the local and global structures of hyperspectral data, accounting for the complex reflectance curve variations between different cultivars. The primary UMAP-boosted model outperformed six mainstream machine learning and deep learning models—including PLSR, SVR, and NN—achieving the highest R 2 values and lowest RMSE. This framework enables automated clustering and enhances Brix and pH prediction from outdoor hyperspectral data under challenging field conditions. Future work should adapt the sensing platform for varying sunlight intensity and diverse geographical regions.

title: Corrigendum to “Physics-guided GAN and ANN hybrid framework for small-sample performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying device” [Comput. Electron. Agric. 253 (2026) 112064]
Automated homogeneity-check of agricultural parcels using machine learning: increased performance in compliance with EU common agricultural policy
abstract: Accurate assessments of agricultural parcel geometries are crucial for calculating financial subsidies. Today, authorities use aerial images to check parcels for homogeneous cultivation and incorrect parcel geometries (homogeneity-check). Due to the large number of parcels and the limited resources in authority offices, there is a need for an automated method of preselecting a manageable sample of parcels for manual review. To this end, this study introduces (i) a novel method for automated homogeneity-check including (ii) a user utility metric reflecting its ability to preselect presumably heterogeneous parcels, i.e., those that benefit from manual review. The new is metric (ii), called Precision of Prioritized Items (PPI), was used to evaluate the performance of four machine learning approaches for homogeneity checking (i): Image Classification, Semantic Segmentation, Edge Detection, and Clustering. Moreover, the evaluation also assessed the robustness of these approaches regarding image resolution. The results show that all approaches performed similarly in terms of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the PPI metric; Image Classification: AUROC = 77.4%, PPI = 90%, Semantic Segmentation AUROC = 83.0%, PPI = 100%, Edge Detection: AUROC = 79.2%, PPI = 90%, and Clustering: AUROC = 84.4%, PPI = 100%. However, only the Clustering approach consistently maintained a stable PPI of 100%, regardless of image resolution, demonstrating superior robustness. The implementation of the Clustering approach enabled the authorities to improve their performance in this task by 294% from 2023 to 2024.

title: BioLQM: a novel hybrid intelligent model for feed optimization and growth evaluation in juvenile spotted knifejaw (Oplegnathus punctatus)
Multi-site dissolved oxygen prediction using physics-guided graph convolutional network in aquaculture ponds
GeoDaRT: Contextual geospatial data infrastructure for distributed on-farm experimentation
abstract: On-farm experimentation (OFE) is increasingly recognized as a pathway for developing sustainable and context-specific agricultural practices under real-world production conditions. However, OFE outcomes are difficult to interpret, compare, and aggregate when the environmental and biophysical context of each experiment is not described in a consistent and reproducible way. The main barrier is not only access to public geospatial data, but the repeated transformation of heterogeneous soil, terrain, weather, drought, and satellite products into traceable, analysis-ready covariates linked to agricultural fields and experimental time windows. This study presents the Geospatial Data Retrieval Tool (GeoDaRT), a web-based system that implements a reproducible contextual data workflow for OFE and related agricultural research. GeoDaRT organizes retrieval around experiment-oriented requests consisting of an area of interest, temporal parameters, selected data products, and processing options. The workflow standardizes access, clipping, file formatting, naming, metadata, packaging, and provenance while preserving native source resolution and coordinate reference information where appropriate. GeoDaRT was evaluated through a distributed field-scale analytical-readiness workload involving 200 corn and soybean fields in New York State and the U.S. Midwest over three growing seasons. The system produced 105,984 contextual files representing 600 site-years. These outputs supported an end-to-end multivariate analysis of 19,900 field pairs without custom reformatting. The analytical-readiness workload produced a coherent contextual feature space and demonstrated that GeoDaRT outputs could support residual-tail summaries and mapped interpretation. These results demonstrate that GeoDaRT makes contextual covariate generation more feasible, auditable, and reusable for distributed OFE.

A mathematical model for land reform planning: A cutting and packing approach with regular plots
abstract: Land reform is a pivotal issue in Brazil, playing a key role in fostering territorial organization, promoting social equity, driving economic development, and preserving traditional landscapes. Despite its importance, effective territorial planning faces significant challenges due to diverse factors, including property size, topography, environmental constraints, infrastructure, and societal needs. This study introduces a mathematical model based on the cutting and packing problem to aid in the subdivision of lands designated for land reform projects. The model takes into account different soil aptitudes, a desired number of assigned plots, and a minimum productivity level for each plot. Two approaches are considered: maximizing land coverage, and minimizing the maximum productivity of the plots while ensuring a minimum coverage, to balance productivity among plots. Through a set of computational experiments, we obtained solutions that can be used as a practical initial approximation for addressing agrarian reform projects. The resulting properties have rectangular shapes and exhibit good balance, equity, and connectivity. Our study promotes the UN’s sustainable development goals, particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), 8 (Decent work and economic growth) and 10 (Reduced inequalities).

A novel model for precise segmentation and disease diagnosis of economic forest images in complicated backgrounds
abstract: Dense cultivation of economic trees, along with cluttered backgrounds of bare soil and overgrown weeds, presents significant challenges for accurate canopy segmentation and disease identification from low-altitude UAV images. To solve this problem, this study developed a Haar-UNet based framework for ginkgo canopy segmentation and leaf disease classification, enabling pixel-level recognition of healthy leaves and four disease types in Ginkgo biloba . The proposed model was enhanced by integrating multi-scale convolution (MSC), squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention mechanisms, and Haar wavelet downsampling (HWD). On the test set, the Haar-UNet canopy segmentation model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 93.53% and a pixel accuracy (PA) of 97.92%. Haar-UNet outperformed six other regularly used semantic segmentation models, with an average gain of 5.66% in mIoU and 1.86% in PA. The leaf disease classification model, Haar-DiseaseNet, achieved 95.96% accuracy (Acc) with 0.01 Loss. In compared to commonly used classification models, it improved average Acc by 7.22% and reduced average Loss by 57.52%. These findings show that the Haar-UNet-based canopy semantic segmentation and disease classification framework can identify diseases accurately even in densely planted areas with complicated background interference. The proposed approach can support disease monitoring in Ginkgo biloba plantations and provide a valuable reference for identifying diseases in other economic forests by drone photography.

title: Hwc-YOLOv8n-based optimal harvest-plane estimation and combing-brushing mechanism pose synthesis for Hangzhou white chrysanthemum
An explainable deep learning-integrated decision support system for field diagnosis and management of botrytis grey mold in castor
abstract: Botrytis grey mold (BGM) is one of the most economically damaging diseases of castor, causing severe spike infection and substantial yield losses under conducive field conditions. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support framework that integrates deep-learning based disease diagnosis with four years of operationally validated fungicide efficacy experiments. Multiple machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) algorithms were evaluated for automated BGM detection. Traditional ML models achieved 90–97% accuracy, with a shallow artificial neural network performing best among ML approaches. Deep-learning architectures consistently outperformed ML models, with the Inception Network achieving the highest classification performance (accuracy = 0.97; precision = 0.98; recall = 0.98; F1-score = 0.98; AUC = 1.00). Confusion matrix analysis showed that Inception produced the lowest misclassification rate (9 errors), compared with CNN + Softmax (27) and VGG16 (15). McNemar’s test confirmed the statistically significant superiority of Inception over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 13.13, p < 0.001) and the improved performance of VGG16 over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 4.27, p = 0.039). Explainability analysis using Grad-CAM confirmed biologically meaningful learning, with more than 90% of high-activation regions overlapping with BGM lesions, while t-SNE visualisation revealed clear separation between healthy and infected samples. Learning-curve analysis demonstrated stable convergence of accuracy (0.94–0.98) and precision (0.95–1.00) without overfitting. The trained Inception model was deployed through a web-based decision support system for real-time field diagnosis. Four-year field trials identified propiconazole at 2.0–2.5 ml l − 1 as the most effective treatment, consistently achieving low disease severity (9–12%), high yield gains (108–182%), and superior economic returns (B:C ratio = 2.7–2.8). Yield modelling revealed a strong negative relationship between disease severity and yield (r = −0.98), with an estimated yield loss of 13.4 kg ha⁻1 per 1% increase in disease intensity. Overall, this study presents an interpretable, field-validated AI-driven decision support system for accurate BGM diagnosis and evidence-based fungicide management in castor.

title: Toward autonomous inspection in livestock environments: A multi-sensor semantic SLAM framework for pigsty patrol robots
Postharvest moisture-level classification using LiDAR point clouds: Integrating 3D structure and spectral intensity
abstract: Moisture content plays a decisive role in the postharvest quality and preservation of horticultural produce. Most non-invasive sensing methods capture either spectral or spatial features, failing to account for structural heterogeneity in fresh tissue and introduced during moisture loss. In this work, a dual wavelengths 3D LiDAR sensor was employed for moisture classification in broccoli and mushrooms. The dataset is comprising spatial coordinates and reflectance intensities at 1320 nm, 1450 nm, and a combined moisture index. Samples include paired ground-truth labels for core and periphery regions, with moisture content categorized into high, medium, and low levels. Results show that by using only reflectance intensity features, the baseline models achieve moderate moisture-level classification performance, with accuracies not exceeding 0.82. Combining geometry with reflectance, particularly at 1450 nm and moisture index, PointNet++ yields the most accurate predictions, achieving up to 0.93 accuracy. Geometric features alone offer limited class discriminability, but contribute to prediction robustness across structurally diverse samples. Spatial generalization experiments reveal an asymmetry: models trained on dense, homogeneous core segments generalize effectively to peripheral regions, whereas those trained on periphery segments exhibit reduced accuracy when evaluated on core data. Modality perturbation shows that intensity provides the dominant moisture-sensitive signal, particularly at 1450 nm, while geometry contributes complementary cues that stabilize predictions. At 1320 nm, showing low spectral sensitivity to moisture, reliable classification requires joint use of both modalities. These findings establish LiDAR as an efficient non-invasive moisture monitoring tool in heterogeneous agricultural products. Code: github.com/majharB/vegPoint .
